title: In 58 awake mice, visual areas share trial-to-trial activity through low-dimensional subspaces, and cortical pairs with denser axons use more dimensions at matched strength
abstract: Question: do mouse visual areas communicate through a low-dimensional, misaligned 'communication subspace' (Semedo et al. 2019), and does axonal wiring set its strength or its dimension? Data: Allen Visual Coding Neuropixels, 58 mice in two cohorts (32 primary, 26 replication), 21,658 units in LGd, VISp, VISl, VISrl, LP, VISal, VISpm and VISam, in grey-screen activity, natural scenes, drifting gratings and a natural movie. Method: cross-validated reduced-rank regression from 30 source units to 15 target units on stimulus-free fluctuations, under a plan written before the results. Results: (1) Between areas, the optimal dimension was 2.2 to 3.2, against 4.6 to 6.5 within an area; at matched performance, between-area pairs used 1.6 to 2.3 fewer dimensions in all 7 cohort-condition sets (mouse-bootstrap intervals below 0). With within-area sets at least 40 um apart, the difference was smaller (-0.35 to -1.53; 5 of 7 intervals below 0). (2) The top source PCs gave 74% to 81% of the RRR performance between areas and 78% to 84% within; the between-area loss was larger in all sets. (3) Knox axon density did not clearly predict strength over all 56 directed pairs (r 0.09 to 0.30), but it predicted the dimension at matched strength (5 of 7 sets; pooled r 0.34, permutation p 0.003). In an added cortex-only test, the dimension link was r 0.52 to 0.76 (exact p <= 0.018 in all sets) and stayed after control for area distance (pooled partial r 0.57, p 0.0014). (4) Feedforward and feedback directions did not differ consistently. (5) A subspace fitted in one condition gave 66% to 79% of within-condition performance in another (random subspaces 16% to 27%). Limitations: tracer wiring from other mice; only 8 structures; the cortex-only and distance tests were added after the planned results; receptive-field overlap was not controlled. Allen data are not included; code, aggregate tables and retrieval instructions are.
